text:
maria: FYI — PrivEdge EU wants to remove the bastion and use a VPN + jump-serviceless model. Need a quick run at RBAC, audit, and KMS implications. Who can triage?

devon: whoa — do we have a design doc? that changes our assumption for jumpbox auth flows.

amaria: minimal doc in PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/privedge/merge/37 — but it's rough. main asks: no permanent bastion, all access via ephemeral VPN certs + ssh-agent forwarding blocked.

sam: checklist thought: 1) ensure KMS decrypt calls from node agents use scoped svcacc 2) prohibit metadata server egress for keys 3) audit log pipeline captures node->kms events and is immutable for 90d 4) netpols deny all egress except metrics/siem endpoints

alex: +1. Also: RBAC change: remove team-admin ssh group, introduce short-lived role binding via OPA/AD connector. Need a migration plan to avoid breaking SRE oncall.

maria: exact ask from customer: "we need isolation guarantees comparable to bastion with lower ops overhead". They care about lateral movement, keystore exposure, and forensic trail.

devon: for keystore: can we use HSM-backed keys per-customer? or at least separate KEK per cluster?

sam: we can insist on separate KMS keys per tenant in PrivEdge. Implementation: node-agent authenticates with workload identity to get a short-term data-key via KMS. No long-lived decrypt perms on node.

alex: on audit: push KMS audit events to dedicated SIEM index and add a checksum chain to detect tamper. retention 90/180/365 options.

maria: network policy prototype? Sam, can you paste the snippet you mentioned earlier so we can show the customer?

sam: sure — quick NetPolicy example (deny-by-default egress, allow only metrics + siem + kms endpoints):

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: privedge-egress-lockdown
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.0.0/16  # cluster internal infra
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: siem
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 9200
```

alex: we'll need to add egress for KMS endpoints (regional) and for cert authority endpoints (vpn cert provisioning). Keep a small allowlist.

maria: question: how do we ensure KMS calls are auditable when node agents get short-lived creds? can we correlate svcacc->pod->user?

sam: yes — add structured audit metadata to KMS calls: include `x-rw-pod`, `x-rw-cluster`, and ephemeral token id. Ship those fields to SIEM and link to the kube-audit records. Also include svcacc fingerprint in the event.

devon: are there perf implications for every decrypt requiring KMS? some workflows decrypt model keys frequently.

sam: for model-serving keys we rely on envelope encryption and a local ephemeral data-key cache (TTL short e.g., 5m) and rotate per workload. The KMS only unwraps the DEK, not every token. That keeps latency ok.

alex: vuln triage: if KMS creds leak, blast radius limited by short TTL + per-cluster key scoping. But we must ensure rollback path: ability to revoke keys and rotate DEKs without downtime. add runbook.

maria: can infra-bot generate a starter runbook and a canary playbook for key revocation?

infra-bot: runbook created: https://runbooks.internal/rb/privedge-bastionless-kms-rotation — includes steps for revoke/rotate, SIEM queries, and postmortem checklist :white_check_mark:

maria: good. last item: RBAC migration for oncall. we need a small window to migrate to ephemeral role bindings. propose: staged rollout: dev cluster -> staging -> prod-canary (10% nodes) -> prod. Can we automate role bind teardown if no login traces after 72h?

devon: automation OK. OPA policy + controller can garbage collect rolebindings after 72h if unused. Need a safe override.

sam: I'll open an infra PR with the OPA policy + netpol + KMS key scoping doc. estimate: 3 sprints to reach canary.

maria: thanks — please add the migration timeline and a short customer-facing summary (1 pager) for EU PrivEdge. I'll shepherd approvals.

alex: tagging security review: @sam @devon please flag any residual risks in the PR.

deploy-bot: new checklist attached to PR 3812: security-review-needed

maria: ack. I'll schedule a 30m sync with the customer next Tue to walk the plan. :calendar: 

devon: thanks — will test netpol in staging and report back by EOD Friday.

sam: noted — I'll push the PR draft today.

maria: closing loop — great progress, keeping this thread for audit trace. :lock:
